title: How Damon Chen went from a lonely-dev side project to Testimonial and full time
summary: Damon Chen explains how he pivoted a video community (lonely.dev) into Testimonial by reusing most of the code, launched fast on Product Hunt with a lifetime deal, and quit his Cisco job in public at $1K MRR. He also covers why he took calm fund money as a solo founder and how to tell if money or product-market fit is your blocker.

principles.text: Pivot a project into a new product by reusing code you already shipped, to cut opportunity and time cost.
principles.quote: The best use case for me is to just reuse the code that I previously shipped to lonely dev and try to see if I can pivot into a standalone product.

principles.text: Build what solves your own selling problem: social proof is a universal need for indie hackers.
principles.quote: how can I sell the product? How can I get the social proof and prove that potential buyers that, hey, this is the legit and you can buy it.

principles.text: Launch fast: ship an MVP in about a week, launch on Product Hunt the next day, and use a lifetime deal for early cash.
principles.quote: I can quickly build the MVP within a week. I launch it, I directly launch it, after the MVP is done, the next day I launched it on product hunt.

principles.text: Early revenue is the strongest validation and motivation.
principles.quote: I would say the, uh, stripe notification is the thing about, you know, energized me during the first few launch days.

principles.text: Set a public revenue milestone to quit your job and agree the downside with your family up front.
principles.quote: if I can reach a 1000 MRR, I'm going to quit, quit my job in public.

principles.text: Identify what actually blocks you from going full time: if it is money, take funding; if it is product-market fit, validate first.
principles.quote: you got to know what is the thing that blocks you from really quitting our job? You know, I mean, if it is money, take the money.
